title: Will it fit through the door?
hook: Which face clears the pictured opening?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that a doorway only tests the item's two dimensions that face the opening, so turning a box to lead with its narrow face can make it fit while its volume stays the same

misconception: If an item is smaller in volume than the space it is going to, it will go through the door.
objective: An object can have a small volume yet fail an opening. This drawing compares a rigid box’s two widths with the clear doorway width. Turning it changes the blocking dimension.

claims.text: Fit depends on the width that meets the opening, not on volume. 90 cm fails a 75 cm doorway; turning the box so a 70 cm or 50 cm side meets it leaves clearance. Corners and height need their own checks.

recall.question: A rigid box is 90 × 70 × 50 cm. The doorway is 75 cm wide. Ignoring height and corners, what gets it through?
options: Turn it so a narrower side meets the opening
Nothing: the box's volume is too large
Push it with the 90 cm side across the opening
recall.why: Fit depends on the width that meets the opening, not on volume. 90 cm fails a 75 cm doorway; turning the box so a 70 cm or 50 cm side meets it leaves clearance. Corners and height need their own checks.
